reading.body:
The directory counts 450 tools across 23 categories, but only 63 have in-depth profiles covering pricing, strengths, weaknesses, and governance.

The gap between 450 and 63 is the real finding. A catalog this broad can list what exists, but depth is reserved for a seventh of it. Governance notes in particular appear only in the profiled subset, so for most of the 450 tools the directory records presence, not accountability.

For AI specifically, that asymmetry matters because tool selection is now a procurement and compliance decision, not just a capability comparison. Buyers need pricing and governance detail to justify a choice, and those are exactly the fields the unprofiled majority lacks.

The data does not say which categories the 63 profiles fall into, how the 450 were selected, or whether the count is growing. It also carries no compute, building, or power figures, so it cannot speak to what these tools cost to run or where they run.
